title: Applying Machine Learning Algorithms to Improve the Accuracy of Medium- to Long-Term Sand and Dust Storm Forecasting
institution: University of Science and Technology Beijing (北京科技大学)

scenes.title: Scene 1: Research Formulation & Title
scenes.voiceover: Welcome to the research presentation on applying machine learning algorithms to improve the accuracy of medium- to long-term sand and dust storm forecasting. Sand and dust storms represent severe atmospheric hazards across arid and semi-arid regions of East Asia. This study, conducted at the University of Science and Technology Beijing, addresses the critical predictability gap at sub-seasonal to seasonal horizons, specifically from 3 to 15 days up to monthly trends. By integrating multi-modal observations, reanalysis data, and physics-constrained deep learning architectures, we establish an end-to-end framework to transform hazard warning from reactive emergency response to proactive scientific defense.
key_points: Research Title: Applying ML Algorithms for Medium- to Long-Term SDS Forecasting
Academic Institution: University of Science and Technology Beijing (USTB)
Target Horizons: Extended-range 3 to 15 days, sub-seasonal and monthly trends
Core Mission: Multi-modal fusion & physics-constrained deep learning architectures
Strategic Goal: Shifting hazard management from reactive response to proactive defense

scenes.title: Scene 2: Climate Change Drivers in China
scenes.voiceover: China is experiencing pronounced environmental shifts that alter dust storm frequency and intensity. First, extreme warming across the Mongolian Plateau and northern China causes rapid topsoil drying, making loose sediments easily mobilized into the air. Second, severe precipitation deficits and below-average snow cover throughout the Gobi Desert and Inner Mongolia deplete surface moisture. Third, more active spring Mongolian cyclones create intense gale-force wind systems capable of lifting massive dust plumes across thousands of kilometers. Furthermore, land degradation and agricultural expansion have stripped natural vegetative soil anchors, while long-term ecological projects such as the Three-North Shelter Forest are frequently overwhelmed by acute regional climate anomalies, as evidenced by the severe Harbin darkening events.
key_points: Extreme Warming: Rapid temperature rise drying out Mongolian Plateau topsoil
Moisture Deficits: Depleted spring snow cover & rainfall in Gobi & Inner Mongolia
Cyclonic Forcing: High-velocity spring Mongolian cyclones lifting transboundary plumes
Ecological Stress: Land degradation vs. afforestation defenses overwhelmed by anomalies
Regional Extremes: Dramatic May and June storm surges turning northern cities pitch-dark

scenes.title: Scene 3: Causes & Physical Mechanisms of SDS
scenes.voiceover: Sand and dust storm initiation is governed by complex land-atmosphere couplings. Major source regions, including the vast Taklimakan Desert in northwestern China and the Gobi Desert across northern China and Mongolia, provide an abundant reservoir of fine mineral dust. When strong cold fronts and baroclinic atmospheric systems sweep across these arid expanses, surface friction velocity exceeds aerodynamic threshold levels, lifting fine sediments into the boundary layer. The availability of erodible particles is tightly coupled to antecedent conditions over days, months, and seasons, including soil moisture, surface roughness, temperature anomalies, and prolonged drought. Consequently, dust storms cannot be modeled as isolated instantaneous events, but as cross-scale physical phenomena driven by delayed environmental memory.
key_points: Primary Sources: Vast sediment reservoirs in Taklimakan Desert and Gobi Desert
Trigger Dynamics: Spring cold fronts, baroclinic systems & aerodynamic friction threshold
Cross-Scale Memory: 1-to-12-month antecedent drought & soil moisture controls
Nonlinear Couplings: Vegetation phenology and soil moisture governing sediment erodibility
Forecast Horizon: Requires incorporating delayed environmental memory into AI models

scenes.title: Scene 4: Multi-Scale Impacts & Public Health
scenes.voiceover: Sandstorms pose extraordinary challenges to societal operations and public health worldwide, impacting over 330 million people in 151 nations. In northern and eastern China, severe events cause near-zero visibility, plunging cities into daytime darkness, grounding commercial aviation, and causing catastrophic traffic disruption. High airborne concentrations of PM10 and PM2.5 trigger severe respiratory and cardiovascular morbidity. Epidemiological findings published in Nature Communications demonstrate substantial increases in hospital admissions and cause-specific mortality during dust outbreaks. Furthermore, toxic oxidative-potential components and persistent free radicals carried by mineral particles cause cellular damage, while deposition across agricultural zones ruins crop yields and exacerbates desertification.
key_points: Global Reach: Over 330 million people affected across 151 countries worldwide
Transportation Shutdown: Near-zero daytime visibility, flight groundings, highway closures
Public Health Risk: Spikes in PM10 & PM2.5, respiratory & cardiovascular mortality
Biochemical Toxicity: Mineral dust carries oxidative-potential components & free radicals
Agricultural Damage: Farmland topsoil erosion, crop burial, and accelerated desertification

scenes.title: Scene 5: Traditional NWP & Bottlenecks
scenes.voiceover: Operational dust forecasting has traditionally relied on numerical weather prediction models and chemical transport simulations. While these physical systems capture synoptic dynamics, they face critical operational bottlenecks. Initial atmospheric condition uncertainties, empirical dust-emission parameterizations, and boundary-layer turbulence approximations lead to rapid error accumulation. Because atmospheric flow is chaotic, numerical forecast accuracy decays sharply beyond 48 to 72 hours, rendering 3-to-15-day sub-seasonal forecasting highly unreliable. Furthermore, running multi-scale physical ensembles demands enormous computational resources, leaving emergency agencies with a post-event response posture rather than true proactive lead time.
key_points: Physical Basis: Synoptic atmospheric transport & chemical dispersion modeling
Critical Bottlenecks: Emission parameterization errors & boundary-layer uncertainties
Predictability Barrier: Rapid chaotic error compounding beyond 48 to 72 hours
Computational Barrier: Enormous computational cost preventing dense real-time ensembles
Operational Result: Reliance on passive post-event responses instead of early warning

scenes.title: Scene 6: The AI Revolution in Earth Systems
scenes.voiceover: Machine learning offers a transformative paradigm to overcome the limitations of classical numerical prediction. By extracting high-dimensional nonlinear patterns from petabytes of satellite, surface, and atmospheric data, modern AI models learn complex relationships without rigid mathematical assumptions. Breakthrough systems such as AI-GAMFS and Google's NeuralGCM have demonstrated that data-driven architectures can match or exceed traditional atmospheric models in speed and precision. In sandstorm forecasting, machine learning models effectively integrate multi-modal heterogeneous inputs, identify slowly varying environmental memory signals, and correct systematic numerical biases.
key_points: Data-Driven Paradigm: Mining high-dimensional nonlinear Earth observation records
Frontier Milestones: AI-GAMFS and Google NeuralGCM show AI prowess in weather modeling
Multi-Modal Integration: Fusing ground stations, satellite retrievals & reanalysis tensors
Systematic Error Correction: Learning and eliminating numerical model biases
Extended Horizon: Harnessing slowly varying climate memory for sub-seasonal outlooks

scenes.title: Scene 7: Deep Learning Spatiotemporal Models
scenes.voiceover: To capture both temporal persistence and spatial advection, our research investigates a comprehensive hierarchy of advanced deep learning architectures. For time-series dependencies, Long Short-Term Memory networks and Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Units with attention mechanisms retain multi-day environmental forcing. To model continuous spatial dust advection, Convolutional Neural Networks and Spatiotemporal Transformers capture multi-scale atmospheric flow fields. Most crucially, Graph Neural Networks represent the geographic topography and spatial propagation network of dust source regions, tracking plume transport along realistic meteorological corridors. For tabular and ensemble post-processing, gradient boosting models including XGBoost, CatBoost, and LightGBM provide robust bias correction.
key_points: Recurrent Sequence Models: LSTM & Bi-GRU with attention for long-term temporal memory
Spatiotemporal Attention: Transformers capture cross-scale atmospheric correlations
Graph Neural Networks (GNN): Message passing across spatial dust propagation networks
Gradient Boosting Ensembles: XGBoost, CatBoost & LightGBM for numerical post-processing
Multi-Scale Representation: Jointly learning local emission thresholds and regional advection

scenes.title: Scene 8: Physics-Informed ML & Interpretability
scenes.voiceover: Pure data-driven models risk making unphysical predictions under extreme out-of-distribution conditions. To ensure physical validity, we incorporate physics-informed neural network principles by embedding atmospheric constraints, such as mass conservation and aerodynamic threshold friction velocities, directly into network loss functions. To ensure operational credibility for meteorologists, we employ Explainable AI methodologies. Using SHAP value attributions and neural attention weight visualizations, we quantitatively isolate the exact influence of soil moisture, wind shear, upstream dust loading, and surface roughness on every forecast decision, ensuring the model is trustworthy and scientifically sound.
key_points: Physics-Informed Constraints: Embedding mass conservation & threshold friction velocity
Physical Consistency: Constrained optimization prevents unphysical out-of-distribution output
SHAP Value Attribution: Decomposing contributions of soil moisture, wind shear & temperature
Attention Weight Heatmaps: Visualizing active dust transport corridors for forecasters
Trust & Transparency: Enhancing scientific interpretability and operational adoption

scenes.title: Scene 9: Methodology & 5-Step Pipeline
scenes.voiceover: The core methodology is structured around five systematic steps evaluated across four benchmark meteorological stations in China. Step 1 acquires and harmonizes multi-source data from ECMWF, China Meteorological Administration stations, ERA5 reanalysis, and MODIS satellite retrievals. Step 2 constructs three feature tiers: surface emission conditions, dynamic transport features, and historical upstream memory. Step 3 develops our dual-track modeling framework: Line A for numerical bias correction and Line B for end-to-end spatiotemporal risk forecasting. Step 4 resolves extreme event class imbalance using SMOTE oversampling, cost-sensitive focal loss, and probability calibration. Step 5 conducts multi-metric validation using Threat Scores, ROC-AUC, and retrospective severe storm case studies.
key_points: Data Integration: ECMWF, CMA 4 stations, ERA5 reanalysis & MODIS satellite tensors
3-Tier Feature Engineering: Emission conditions, atmospheric transport & upstream memory
Dual-Track Modeling: Line A (NWP Bias Correction) + Line B (End-to-End Deep Spatiotemporal)
Class Imbalance Handling: SMOTE oversampling, cost-sensitive focal loss & calibration
Comprehensive Validation: Threat Score (TS), ETS, ROC-AUC, and severe event case studies

scenes.title: Scene 10: Milestones, Deliverables & Impact
scenes.voiceover: Spanning September 2025 through June 2027, the research roadmap culminates in a validated, operational-ready forecasting system and master's dissertation defense. The expected deliverables include high-resolution 3-to-15-day risk probability maps, an open benchmark dataset, and publication in top-tier environmental informatics journals. By extending warning lead times up to five full days, this intelligent framework empowers aviation scheduling, civil protection, and solar and wind energy infrastructure. In summary, uniting physics-informed AI with multi-source Earth observations will advance China's capacity to anticipate sandstorms and protect human communities. Thank you for your attention.
key_points: 7 Research Phases: September 2025 to June 2027 concluding with USTB thesis defense
Core Deliverables: 3 to 15 day probabilistic risk grids, open benchmark & publications
Civil Resilience: 5-day warning window protecting aviation, public health & green energy
Decisive Shift: Moving environmental meteorology toward proactive AI resilience
Department: USTB School of Energy and Environmental Engineering
